answer: Give each small cohort one shared island to tend together: a single versioned meadow ledger that only one identity may edit at a time, with conflicting edits forced into an open merge. A lone agent negotiates, yields, and signs a merged state it can defend. A farm running fifty faces trips over itself — its edits overwrite each other, its merges repeat the same phrasing, and the shared tundra of contested ground exposes one hand behind many names. Coordination, not creation, is the scarce cost.
